overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts data reveals that extreme cosmic anomalies and hypothetical 'What If' scenarios featuring planetary extremes (e.g., diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) drive the highest velocity in views-per-day and engagement-per-view compared to standard biology facts or psychological tricks. Videos published within the last 7 to 30 days significantly outperform older catalog items in relative daily traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like IYuce8vaU3Y ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') and v1rrcZLdp4U ('The Planet Darker Than Coal') generated over 1,000 views rapidly with strong like-per-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes cosmic 'What If' scenarios and bizarre exoplanet weather conditions.

winning_patterns.evidence: A9Qa-RmuOr0 ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year 🤯') achieved nearly 1,000 views and 21 likes efficiently by combining a mind-bending temporal fact with expressive punctuation.
winning_patterns.action: Use counter-intuitive physics/astronomy contrasts paired with curiosity-inducing emojis in titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: ef3ND4qiRHc and 5AN7LUgqarc received minimal daily traction and low view counts relative to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological micro-tips unless paired with a dramatic biological hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: AXAfwrzzEdU and 1Bm0zw_qAAg ('Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') showed flat, stagnant long-term growth after initial spikes.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid repeating standard animal trivia; pivot animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary adaptations.

Must use a newly introduced celestial element (Liquid Neon star).

experiment: Test a 21-second narrative structure on an undiscovered exoplanet extreme to measure whether increased watch time improves algorithmic push over the 16-second baseline.
